_reasons.engine/src/application/jce_runtime.c: 5167 -> 5295: the world-vs-local wiring, at the EIGHT sites in this file that read or wrote a physics pose through the raw JceTransform -- the spawn walk, the push pass, the pull pass, the character pull, the soft-body centre, the nav agent, the vehicle chassis and client-side prediction. 101 of the 128 lines are comments, and they are the deliverable as much as the code is: every one of these sites LOOKED correct, compiles either way, and is wrong only for a parented entity, which is why the defect survived in three directions at once. The canonical explanation is written ONCE at rt_spawn_entity and the other seven cite it rather than restate it -- an earlier draft repeated it and was 14 lines longer. Splitting the file was considered and does not apply: these are edits inside existing functions, not new ones, so there is nothing to move to a new translation unit.  ||  5295 -> 5321: 5295 -> 5321: the on_fixed_update dispatch loop and the 21 lines that say why it is HERE. Two accumulators unified by clock are not thereby guaranteed to agree on step count in a given frame, so the callback dispatches INLINE immediately before jce_physics_step rather than off JCE_PHASE_FIXED_UPDATE -- which exists, and which coroutines already use for WaitForFixedUpdate. jce_player_loop.h says in its own header that the phases are an AUXILIARY surface firing alongside the inline pipeline; this accumulator is inline. A script force applied a different number of times than physics steps is the exact bug this callback exists to prevent, so the ordering is the feature and not an implementation detail. The comment also records that the loop is NOT sim-LOD gated, unlike on_update directly above it: a fixed-step callback that fires at a distance-dependent rate is a contradiction of its own contract. Without those lines the next reader moves the call to the phase because the phase looks tidier, and nothing fails.  ||  5321 -> 5401: The typed-constraint registry (JointEntry) plus rt_sync_joint_motors. rt_spawn_joint discarded the constraint handle, so a motor could only be set at spawn -- an authoring-time-only motor is a door that is either always opening or never opening.
